reason: E1 and E3 confirm the dual-phase FCC+σ structure and state that galvanic corrosion occurs due to potential difference between phases, and that oxide film rupture occurs during wear, but the cited evidence does not address elevated-temperature simultaneous wear-corrosion, oxide re-formation kinetics, or synergistic feedback between wear and corrosion.
premises: Multiphase eutectic HEA contains chemically/electrochemically distinct phases (FCC + σ/Laves)
Phase potential difference creates localized galvanic cells
Elevated temperature forms protective oxide films on phases
Wear mechanically removes oxide films, exposing fresh material
Oxide removal accelerates both wear and corrosion synergistically
